title: Finite-clopen complex equivalence and unbounded derived localization
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a finite set, and $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on their small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, $R_i=R|_{X_i}$, and let $r_i$, $G$ and $e_i$ be the restriction, sectionwise product gluing, and zero insertion functors of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Use unbounded cochain complexes, quasi-isomorphisms, cohomology and derived localizations $Q_R:\mathrm{CoCh}(R)\to D(R)$ and $Q_{R_i}$ as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Degreewise $r=(r_i)_i$ and $G$ are inverse equivalences on complexes and on homotopy categories. There are natural comparisons $H^m(r_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K)$ and $H^m(e_iL)\cong e_iH^m(L)$ for every integer $m$. A complex or chain map is acyclic or a quasi-isomorphism, respectively, if and only if all its restrictions have that property.

Degreewise restriction and gluing induce inverse triangulated equivalences
$$r_D:D(R)\simeq\prod_{i\in I}D(R_i):G_D,$$
with localization comparisons $r_{D,i}Q_R\cong Q_{R_i}r_i$ and $G_D(\prod_iQ_{R_i})\cong Q_RG$. The equivalence unit, counit and their triangle equations are the localizations of the specified module gluing unit and counit, applied degreewise. If $e_{D,i}$ is the localization of $e_i$, then naturally $r_{D,i}e_{D,i}\cong1$, $r_{D,i}e_{D,j}\cong0$ for $i\ne j$, $\bigoplus_i e_{D,i}r_{D,i}\cong1$ and $G_D((K_i)_i)\cong\bigoplus_i e_{D,i}K_i$. Moreover $H^m(r_{D,i}K)\cong r_iH^m(K)$ naturally on derived objects and morphisms; the $r_{D,i}$ jointly detect zero objects and isomorphisms.

An empty component has zero complex and derived categories, the latter equivalent to the category with one object and one arrow. The same holds for a zero coefficient sheaf. If $I=\varnothing$, then $X=\varnothing$ and the displayed equivalence is between zero categories.

proof.text: Restriction preserves finite limits by comparison with precomposition of underlying presheaves, and finite colimits by the map/pullback module pushforward adjunction. Package the fully specified sectionwise gluing equivalence with its original unit and counit in FixedEquivalence, fixing the forward tuple functor. Construct insertion by coordinate zero insertion followed by this gluing functor. Its diagonal restriction is naturally the identity by the module counit; its off-diagonal restrictions are zero. Faithfulness of tuple restriction proves insertion additive; the exact-short-complex detector of lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing and these coordinate identities prove insertion exact. The package avoids repeatedly unfolding nested choice witnesses.

Assemble a tuple of cochain complexes into a complex in the product module category, and apply gluing degreewise. Unassemble after degreewise tuple restriction. Naturality of the specified module unit and counit makes their degreewise maps chain maps; the module triangle equations in each degree give both complex triangle equations. A coordinate homotopy equivalence assembles into a homotopy equivalence, and additive gluing preserves it. Localize at homotopy equivalences using the finite product of homotopy quotient functors. The normalized-localized-equivalence helper descends the exact unit and counit via Localization.Adjunction, proves both normalization equations, and inherits both triangles.

Use the existing exact-functor complex homology comparison for restrictions and insertions. For acyclicity, the short complex at each degree maps to the restricted short complex, so the module exactness detector applies degreewise. For quasi-isomorphisms, conjugate each homology map by its natural comparison and use full faithfulness of the module tuple equivalence to reflect isomorphisms. Thus complex gluing takes tuples of quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, since its composite with restriction is naturally the identity.

The finite product P of the component derived localizations is a localization at tuples of quasi-isomorphisms, including the empty product. Use the already defined exact-functor derived restrictions as the forward functor; their factorization isomorphisms assemble into the required comparison with P. Descend degreewise gluing along P using the quasi-isomorphism detection from the preceding step. This gives G_D and its exact localization comparison.

Apply normalized_localized_equivalence to these derived localization data. Its proof forms the source adjunction from the specified unit and counit, descends it with Localization.Adjunction, and descends the inverses of the unit and counit by Localization.liftNatIso. Localization.natTrans_ext identifies these isomorphisms with the adjunction maps, yielding precisely the two required normalization equations and both triangle equations. Thus the specified module normalization is preserved.

Construct the componentwise product shift using ShiftMkCore and its coordinate zero/addition constraints. Give the product category its componentwise zero object and distinguished triangles. The pretriangulated axioms are coordinatewise, with objects and fillers chosen in each coordinate. Each evaluation functor commutes with shifts and preserves distinguished triangles. The tuple of the existing exact-functor derived restrictions is therefore triangulated. Its inverse inherits its coherent shift structure and preservation of distinguished triangles from the equivalence via Triangulated.Adjunction. Its counit compatibility gives the demanded shift normalization; the zero and addition constraints are exactly the componentwise ones. This avoids a separate mapping-cone computation for G_D.

Use the adopted source library's proved mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso for each restriction. It is natural on all derived morphisms and has the required orientation after inversion. This reuses the already established exact-functor cohomology descent rather than repeating its localization proof.

The adopted derived-functor composition, natural-isomorphism and identity comparisons descend each diagonal module insertion identity. Off-diagonal derived composites are zero by isZero_mapDerivedCategory_obj because their module functors kill all objects. Compare these derived insertions to explicit coordinate insertions followed by G_D using the derived unit and their coordinate identities. In the functor category construct the coordinate-insertion bicone with identity vertex and prove its finite sum of projection-inclusion composites is the identity, including the empty sum. Whisker by the additive gluing equivalence and transport along the insertion comparisons. The total-identity criterion supplies the two claimed bilimit bicones with exactly the prescribed vertices, without a separate preservation-of-limits theorem.

Full faithfulness of the derived tuple equivalence detects isomorphisms; faithfulness and coordinate identity-equals-zero detect zero objects. For an empty component, the module-gluing theorem gives a module category equivalent to PUnit, so every module is zero. For zero coefficient sheaves each module section is zero by Module.subsingleton. Every complex over a zero module category is zero degreewise, and every derived object is isomorphic to Q of such a complex by essential surjectivity. Hence the derived category has unique morphisms and is equivalent to PUnit. An empty partition gives X empty by the original covering clause; the product derived category is also zero by empty elimination. No nonempty-index or boundedness hypothesis is used.

Uses the fully proved module-gluing equivalence, finite-product localization, normalized adjunction descent, componentwise product shifts and triangles, the adopted exact-derived-functor API, explicit total-identity bicones, and degreewise zero-category arguments. No sorry remains.
